sentences.simple: If they did not go, the stories of Morgan, of Camelot and of the magic tree house would all end forever.

parts.text: If he and Annie did not go on their quest,

parts.text: Morgan’s story and the stories of Camelot and all the stories about the magic tree house
parts.meaning: Morgan's story, Camelot's stories and the tree house stories

parts.text: would end forever.
parts.meaning: would all stop forever.

sentences.grammar: "If + past, … would + verb" talks about what will happen if something does not happen (here in Jack's thoughts).

sentences.context: His huge antlers seemed to glow in the cold moonlight.

parts.text: seemed to glow
parts.meaning: looked like they were shining

parts.text: in the cold moonlight.
parts.meaning: in the cold light of the moon.

sentences.grammar: "Seem to + verb" = look as if.

sentences.context: But he galloped on—not even breaking his stride as he started up a rocky slope.
sentences.simple: But the stag kept running fast. He did not even slow down when he started to run up the rocky side of the mountain.

parts.text: But he galloped on
parts.meaning: But the stag kept running fast

parts.text: —not even breaking his stride
parts.meaning: — he did not even slow down

parts.text: as he started up a rocky slope.
parts.meaning: when he began to go up a rocky hill.

sentences.grammar: "Galloped on": "on" = continued. "Break your stride" = change your speed of walking or running.

sentences.context: Not only was his body missing, but the fog beneath the bridge was moving in a wild, spinning whirl.
sentences.simple: Jack could not see his body, and also the fog under the bridge was turning round and round wildly.

parts.text: Not only was his body missing,
parts.meaning: His body could not be seen,

parts.text: but the fog beneath the bridge was moving in a wild, spinning whirl.
parts.meaning: and also the fog under the bridge was turning round wildly.

sentences.grammar: "Not only … but (also) …" joins two things. After "Not only" at the start, the verb comes first: "was his body".

sentences.context: All the dancers looked very young—yet they seemed ancient at the same time.
sentences.simple: All the dancers looked young, but they also seemed very old.

parts.text: All the dancers looked very young
parts.meaning: The dancers all looked very young

parts.text: —yet they seemed ancient
parts.meaning: — but they also seemed very, very old

parts.text: at the same time.
parts.meaning: at the same moment.

sentences.grammar: "Yet" = but.

sentences.context: He let go of the hand of the dancer on his right and threw himself out of the dance—pulling the knight on his left with him.
sentences.simple: He let go of the dancer's hand on his right. He jumped out of the dance and pulled the knight on his left out with him.
sentences.main: He threw himself out of the dance.

parts.text: He let go of the hand of the dancer on his right
parts.meaning: He stopped holding the right-hand dancer's hand

parts.text: and threw himself out of the dance
parts.meaning: and jumped out of the circle

parts.text: —pulling the knight on his left with him.
parts.meaning: — and he pulled the knight on his left out too.

sentences.grammar: "Threw himself" = moved suddenly with all his strength.

sentences.context: You can’t get past them without getting caught up in their dance.
sentences.simple: You cannot pass them unless you join their dance and forget everything.

parts.text: You can’t get past them
parts.meaning: Nobody can pass them

parts.text: without getting caught up in their dance.
parts.meaning: without being trapped in their dance.

sentences.grammar: "Without + -ing" = and you do not … . "Get caught up in" = be pulled into something.

sentences.context: Finally, one by one, each Keeper slunk back into the doorway from which it had come.
sentences.simple: In the end, the monsters went back quietly, one after another, into the doors they came from.

parts.text: Finally, one by one,
parts.meaning: In the end, one after another,

parts.text: each Keeper slunk back
parts.meaning: each monster went back quietly and afraid

parts.text: into the doorway from which it had come.
parts.meaning: into the doorway where it came from.

sentences.grammar: "From which it had come" = "that it had come from". Past perfect ("had come") is for the earlier action.

sentences.context: So I assume he brought you to Camelot hoping that you would offer to go instead.
sentences.simple: So I think Merlin brought you to Camelot because he hoped you would say you wanted to go in the knights' place.

parts.text: So I assume
parts.meaning: So I think

parts.text: he brought you to Camelot
parts.meaning: Merlin brought you to Camelot

parts.text: hoping that you would offer to go instead.
parts.meaning: because he hoped you would say you would go in place of the knights.

sentences.grammar: "Instead" = in place of someone else.

sentences.context: Using his memory and his imagination, Jack kept writing, doing his part to keep the legend of King Arthur, the Knights of the Round Table, Merlin, and Morgan le Fay alive.
sentences.simple: Jack used his memory and imagination and kept writing. In this way he helped keep the legend of King Arthur, his knights, Merlin and Morgan alive.

parts.text: Using his memory and his imagination,
parts.meaning: With his memory and imagination,

parts.text: Jack kept writing,
parts.meaning: Jack went on writing,

parts.text: doing his part to keep the legend of King Arthur, the Knights of the Round Table, Merlin, and Morgan le Fay alive.
parts.meaning: and so he did his part to keep the stories of King Arthur, his knights, Merlin and Morgan alive.

sentences.grammar: "Keep something alive" = make it continue to live. "Kept writing" = continued to write.
